proposals.impact: reduce intro drop-off from 3 of 5 sessions never advancing past load screen
proposals.observation: Of 5 quiz sessions in the 48-hour window, 3 stalled at intro_load and never advanced. Only 2 people pressed start, and neither reached the email capture step. The single highest-leverage structural problem is that the quiz intro page is burning three out of every five visitors before the quiz proper begins. Whatever the intro currently asks or promises is not enough to pull a reader from passive to active.
proposals.proposal: Replace the current quiz intro copy with text that names the quiet, specific tension this ICP actually sits with — the feeling of earning well and still not knowing where it goes — and tells them in plain terms what they will receive at the end (a typed result, a named script pattern, something concrete). The current text is almost certainly a generic "find out your money personality" frame. Make it specific enough that someone who earns £60k and still checks their balance with one eye closed recognises themselves in the first sentence.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality in 3 minutes and get a personalised plan to finally take control of your finances.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. You're not reckless. But something about money still feels like a tab you'd rather not open.

This quiz takes under three minutes. At the end you get a named description of the specific pattern running your financial decisions — not a horoscope, a behavioural read based on decades of research into how people actually think about money.

Joel holds an MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner. The result will tell you something true.

proposals.impact: raise Money Worship open rate toward Money Vigilance baseline by sharpening subject line
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% against 19 sends — the lowest of the three active sequences. Money Vigilance sits at 63.64% on 11 sends. The gap is 26 percentage points. Both sequences go to people who just completed the same quiz flow, so list quality is comparable. The most actionable variable Fred can touch in one file edit is the subject line of Email 1 in the Money Worship sequence.
proposals.proposal: The Money Worship result tends to attract people who tie their sense of safety and worth to accumulating more. Their characteristic anxiety is not "I spend too much" but "no amount ever feels like enough." A subject line that speaks to that specific restlessness — rather than a generic "your result is ready" frame — will pull opens. Write a subject line that names the feeling without diagnosing or lecturing, and a preview text that creates enough honest curiosity to click.
proposals.current_text:

Preview: Here's what your answers reveal about your relationship with money.
proposals.new_text:
Subject: When more money still doesn't feel like enough
Preview: Your quiz result names the pattern — and why hitting the next number rarely quiets it.

proposals.impact: convert blog readers into quiz starts by adding a grounded in-post prompt
proposals.observation: The blog post published today — "How do I budget when I'm secretly worried about losing my income?" — targets an anxiety that maps directly onto the quiz's Money Vigilance and Money Avoidance profiles. The content queue holds only one post in reserve. Blog traffic arriving on this post has no visible prompt to enter the quiz funnel. Given that the quiz is recording zero completions and the blog is the only fresh content asset today, adding an inline, contextually relevant quiz prompt inside this post is the fastest way to feed the top of the quiz funnel without building anything new.
proposals.proposal: Insert a short, grounded prose block roughly two-thirds of the way through the blog post, after the emotional weight of the income-worry topic has landed and before the closing section. The block should feel like a natural extension of the reading experience, not a banner ad. It names what the quiz does in plain terms and gives a direct URL. No hype, no urgency tricks — just an honest offer to the person who is already reading because the title described their week.
proposals.new_text:
If this question came up because you typed it into a search bar at 11pm, that's worth paying attention to.

Joel runs a short quiz — under three minutes — that identifies the specific behavioural pattern shaping how you think about money when you're under pressure. It won't tell you to make a spreadsheet. It will tell you something more useful: why the spreadsheet hasn't worked so far.

You can take it at wayofwealth.co.uk/quiz.

Joel holds an MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner.
